offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (first-third); Class E Felony (fourth); Class D Felony (fifth); Class C Felony (sixth); Class B Felony (seventh+)
penalty_max: 12 months (first); 18 months (second); 2 years (third); 5 years (fourth); 8 years (fifth); 15 years (sixth); 25 years (seventh+)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol
Or while under the influence of any drug
Or with an alcohol concentration of .08 or more
mandatory_minimum: No mandatory minimum (first); 60 days (second); 3 months (third); 6 months (fourth); 1 year (fifth); 18 months (sixth); 30 months (seventh+)
enhancements: Child under 17 in vehicle (additional charge under § 11-1102)
notes: Delaware's DUI statute escalates dramatically with repeat offenses. Fourth offense is a Class E Felony. Lookback period is lifetime. Ignition interlock required for most offenses. Zero tolerance (.02) for drivers under 21.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle while under the influence or with BAC .08+
No prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: No mandatory jail time; completion of course of instruction and rehabilitation; 12-month license revocation
enhancements: BAC .15-.199 (enhanced fine and minimum 30-day license revocation period)
notes: First offense may qualify for first offender election under § 4177(g), which allows reduced penalties and potential expungement after 5 years. Ignition interlock device may be ordered.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (second/third); Class E Felony (fourth); Class D Felony (fifth); Class C Felony (sixth); Class B Felony (seventh+)
penalty_min: 60 days (second); 3 months (third); 6 months (fourth); 1 year (fifth); 18 months (sixth); 30 months (seventh+)
penalty_max: 18 months (second); 2 years (third); 5 years (fourth); 8 years (fifth); 15 years (sixth); 25 years (seventh+)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle while under the influence or with BAC .08+
One or more prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 60 days (second); 3 months (third); 6 months (fourth); 1 year (fifth); 18 months (sixth); 30 months (seventh+)
notes: Lifetime lookback period — all prior DUI convictions count regardless of when they occurred. Fourth DUI is a felony. Mandatory minimums cannot be suspended.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
While under the influence of any drug
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any drug
Or while the person has within the person's blood any amount of an illicit or recreational drug or substance
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: Delaware has a per se drugged driving provision — any amount of illicit substance in blood is sufficient. No impairment showing needed for illicit drugs.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. Second or subsequent offense carries enhanced fine.

statute_title: Leaving the Scene of Accident Resulting in Injury or Death
offense_class: Class E Felony (injury); Class D Felony (serious physical injury); Class C Felony (death)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, serious injury, or death
Defendant failed to stop and provide information and render assistance
notes: Property damage only hit-and-run is an unclassified misdemeanor under § 4201. Injury/death escalates to felony.

statute_title: Vehicular Homicide in the First Degree (DUI-related)
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Caused the death of another person
The DUI was a proximate cause of the death
notes: First-degree vehicular homicide applies to DUI-related deaths. Class B Felony with 2-year mandatory minimum. Second degree (§ 630) covers reckless or negligent vehicular deaths (Class E Felony).

statute_title: Vehicular Homicide in the Second Degree
offense_class: Class E Felony
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
With criminal negligence caused the death of another person
notes: Covers non-DUI vehicular deaths caused by criminal negligence. Class E Felony.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (first/second); Class A Misdemeanor (third+)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
mandatory_minimum: 30 days (if DUI-related suspension, second offense); 60 days (DUI-related, third+)
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Driving on a DUI-related suspension carries mandatory minimum jail time. Third offense is upgraded to Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class E Felony (if creating a risk of death or injury)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A Misdemeanor); 5 years (Class E Felony)
elements: Defendant was operating a motor vehicle
A police officer gave a signal to stop
Defendant willfully failed to stop or fled
enhancements: Creating a risk of death or injury to any person (Class E Felony)
notes: Basic violation is Class A Misdemeanor. Creating risk of death or injury elevates to Class E Felony.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (Schedule I-V, personal use quantity)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Delaware Uniform Controlled Substances Act
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school, park, or church (§ 4767, enhanced penalties)
notes: Delaware reformed drug possession in 2015. Simple possession of personal use quantities is a misdemeanor for all schedules. Marijuana under 1 oz. was decriminalized to a civil fine in 2015.

offense_class: Civil violation (under 1 oz.); Unclassified Misdemeanor (1-175g); Class B Felony (175g+)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
In excess of legal personal use quantity or without authorization
enhancements: Near a school, park, or church
notes: Delaware legalized recreational marijuana for adults 21+ in 2023 (HB 1). Possession of up to 1 oz. is legal. Over 1 oz. but under 175g is a misdemeanor. Over 175g may be charged as trafficking.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (personal use); Class E Felony (Tier 1 quantity)
elements: Defendant possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Near a school, park, or church
notes: Personal use quantity is a misdemeanor. Tier quantities trigger trafficking charges under § 4753A.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (personal use); Class E Felony (Tier 1 quantity)
elements: Defendant possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Near a school, park, or church
notes: Same tier system as cocaine. Manufacturing carries separate, harsher penalties.

offense_class: Class E Felony (Tier 1); Class D Felony (Tier 2); Class C Felony (Tier 3); Class B Felony (Tier 4); Class A Felony (Tier 5)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance in a quantity meeting tier thresholds
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory minimums vary by tier and substance
enhancements: Near a school, park, or church
notes: Delaware uses a 5-tier system for drug dealing/trafficking based on weight. Tier 5 is a Class A Felony. Cocaine: Tier 1=5-50g, Tier 2=50-100g, Tier 3=100-500g, Tier 4=500g-2.5kg, Tier 5=2.5kg+.

offense_class: Class E Felony (most); Class D Felony (narcotic Schedule I/II); Class F Felony (Schedule III-V)
penalty_max: 5 years (Class E); 8 years (Class D); 3 years (Class F)
elements: Defendant delivered or sold a controlled substance
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Delivery to a minor (§ 4761, enhanced penalty)
Delivery near a school, park, or church (§ 4767)
notes: Delaware uses 'delivery' and 'dealing.' Delivery to a minor or near protected areas carries enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Class D Felony (most); Class C Felony (meth manufacturing)
elements: Defendant manufactured, created, or produced a controlled substance
Or possessed precursors with intent to manufacture
Without lawful authority
notes: Manufacturing meth is enhanced to Class C Felony. Separate provisions for clandestine lab cleanup costs.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use it for a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (Class F Felony)
notes: Possession is an unclassified misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor is a Class F Felony. Cannabis paraphernalia is legal for adults 21+ following legalization.

offense_class: Class E Felony (most); Class D Felony (narcotic Schedule I/II)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to deliver
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Near a school, park, or church (§ 4767)
notes: Intent can be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, and other circumstantial evidence.

offense_class: Class A Felony
penalty_min: Life without parole (or death if aggravating circumstances, though Delaware's death penalty is unconstitutional per Rauf v. State)
elements: Defendant intentionally caused the death of another person
After a period of premeditation and deliberation
Or while engaged in the commission of certain felonies (felony murder)
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment without possibility of parole
enhancements: Felony murder (during arson, kidnapping, rape, robbery, burglary, escape)
notes: Delaware's death penalty was ruled unconstitutional by the Delaware Supreme Court in Rauf v. State (2016). Maximum sentence is now life without parole.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
Under circumstances manifesting a cruel, wicked, and depraved indifference to human life
notes: Second-degree murder covers depraved-heart killings and intentional killings without premeditation. 15-year mandatory minimum.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
Or intentionally caused the death under circumstances that do not constitute murder due to extreme emotional distress for which there was a reasonable explanation
notes: Delaware's manslaughter statute covers reckless killings and heat-of-passion killings with extreme emotional distress as a mitigating factor.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With criminal negligence
notes: Criminally negligent homicide is a Class D Felony. Lower culpability than manslaughter.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally caused serious physical injury to another person
By means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or recklessly caused serious physical injury under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
notes: First-degree assault is a Class B Felony with a 2-year mandatory minimum. Assault on law enforcement carries additional mandatory minimums.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly caused physical injury to another person
Or with criminal negligence caused physical injury by means of a deadly weapon
notes: Third-degree assault is the base assault offense. Second degree (§ 612) is Class D Felony.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally touched another person
Either with a member of the defendant's body or with any instrument
Knowing that the person would reasonably regard the contact as offensive or provocative
notes: Delaware has 'offensive touching' as a separate lesser offense below assault. Covers what many states call simple battery.

offense_class: Class E Felony
elements: Defendant committed a theft
Defendant used or threatened the immediate use of force upon another person
For the purpose of preventing resistance to the taking or retaining
notes: Second-degree robbery is the base offense. First degree (§ 832) involves a deadly weapon, serious injury, or display of what appears to be a deadly weapon (Class B Felony).

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant committed a robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or threatened use of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
Or caused physical injury to non-participant
enhancements: Use of a firearm (mandatory additional time)
notes: Class B Felony with 2-year mandatory minimum. First-degree robbery is a violent felony under Delaware law.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant unlawfully restrained another person
With intent to hold for ransom, use as a shield or hostage, facilitate a felony, inflict physical injury, terrorize, or interfere with governmental function
notes: First-degree kidnapping is a Class A Felony with 15-year mandatory minimum. Second degree (§ 783) is a Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged a building
By starting a fire or causing an explosion
When another person whose presence was reasonably foreseeable was present
notes: First-degree arson requires person present. Second degree (§ 802, Class D Felony) covers buildings. Third degree (§ 801, Class E Felony) covers property.

statute_title: Attempted Murder in the First Degree
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant intended to cause the death of another person
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of murder
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempt to commit a Class A Felony is a Class B Felony. One of the most serious attempt charges.

statute_title: Assault in the First Degree — With Deadly Weapon
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally caused serious physical injury to another
By means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument
notes: Class B Felony with 2-year mandatory minimum. Deadly weapon defined broadly.

offense_class: Class F Felony ($1,500+); Class G Felony ($1,000-$1,500); Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
penalty_max: 3 years (Class F); 2 years (Class G); 1 year (Class A Misd.)
elements: Defendant took, exercised control over, or obtained the property of another person
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Delaware uses 'theft' as the general statute. Thresholds: $1,500+ = Class F Felony, $1,000-$1,500 = Class G Felony, under $1,000 = Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class F Felony
elements: Defendant took or exercised control over property
Value exceeds $1,500
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Delaware's felony theft threshold is $1,500. Uses 'theft' terminology rather than 'grand theft.'

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant took or exercised control over property
Value is under $1,000
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Under $1,000 is Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000); Class G Felony ($1,000-$1,500); Class F Felony ($1,500+)
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant concealed or took possession of merchandise
Of a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of value without paying
notes: Delaware has a specific shoplifting statute. Penalties follow the theft value tiers.

offense_class: Class F Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In a building
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Third degree is the base burglary. Second degree (§ 825, Class D Felony) covers dwelling entry. First degree (§ 826, Class C Felony) covers dwelling with weapon, injury, or at night.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully in a dwelling
With intent to commit a crime therein
And was armed with a deadly weapon, caused injury, or used or threatened force
notes: First-degree burglary requires entry into a dwelling with aggravating circumstances. Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class F Felony (most vehicles); Class G Felony (under $1,500 value)
elements: Defendant took or exercised control over a motor vehicle
Without authorization and with intent to deprive the owner
notes: No separate motor vehicle theft statute. Charged as theft based on vehicle value.

offense_class: Same as theft based on value tier
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of stolen property
Knowing that it was stolen or believing it was probably stolen
notes: Same value-tier classification as theft.

offense_class: Class D Felony ($5,000+); Class G Felony ($1,000-$5,000); Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
penalty_max: 8 years (Class D); 2 years (Class G); 1 year (Class A Misd.)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged the property of another
notes: Delaware uses 'criminal mischief.' Degree based on damage amount.

statute_title: Criminal Trespass in the First Degree
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first degree, dwelling); Class B Misdemeanor (second degree, building); Unclassified Misdemeanor (third degree, premises)
penalty_max: 1 year (first degree); 6 months (second degree); 30 days (third degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In a dwelling, building, or upon premises of another
notes: Three degrees. First degree (dwelling) is Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony ($5,000+)
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged property of another
Damage exceeds $5,000
enhancements: Damage to utility or communication property
notes: Over $5,000 damage. Lesser amounts are Class G Felony or misdemeanor.

statute_title: Domestic Violence — Offensive Touching or Assault
offense_class: Depends on underlying offense (offensive touching through first-degree assault)
elements: Defendant committed an act constituting a crime against a family member, former spouse, cohabitant, or dating partner
As defined in 10 Del. C. § 1041
notes: Delaware addresses domestic violence through the general criminal statutes with domestic relationship designation. Mandatory arrest provisions apply. Protection from Abuse orders available under 10 Del. C. § 1041.

offense_class: Class B Felony (first degree); Class D Felony (second degree); Class A Misdemeanor (third degree)
elements: Defendant caused physical injury to a family or household member
With the intent level required for the applicable degree of assault
notes: Domestic battery charged as assault of the applicable degree. Strangulation of a household member is a separate Class D Felony.

statute_title: Endangering the Welfare of a Child
offense_class: Class E Felony (knowing/intentional); Class A Misdemeanor (reckless/negligent)
elements: Defendant knowingly acted in a manner likely to be injurious to the physical, mental, or moral welfare of a child
Child is under 18 years of age
notes: Broadly applied. Includes DUI with a child in the vehicle. Knowing/intentional endangerment is Class E Felony; reckless/negligent is Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class D Felony (physical injury); Class B Felony (serious physical injury)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly caused physical injury to a child
Child is under 18 years of age
Defendant is responsible for the care, custody, or control of the child
notes: Mandatory reporting requirements apply. Serious physical injury elevates to Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class G Felony (second); Class F Felony (third+)
elements: A valid protection from abuse order was in effect
Defendant had notice of the order
Defendant knowingly violated a condition of the order
notes: Escalating penalties with each subsequent violation. Mandatory arrest upon violation.

offense_class: Class G Felony (basic); Class F Felony (aggravated)
elements: Defendant knowingly engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear physical injury or death
Or suffer other significant emotional distress
enhancements: Violation of court order (aggravated, Class F Felony)
notes: Stalking is always a felony in Delaware. Aggravated stalking (in violation of a court order) is Class F Felony.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor (basic); Class A Misdemeanor (aggravated)
elements: Defendant with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Struck, shoved, kicked, or otherwise subjected another to physical contact
Or used obscene language or made an obscene gesture in a public place
notes: Aggravated harassment (§ 1311A) involves repeated acts or credible threats.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of an Adult Who Is Impaired or Infirm
offense_class: Class F Felony (abuse/neglect); Class D Felony (aggravated)
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited an impaired or infirm adult
Defendant had a caretaker relationship
Person is elderly or otherwise unable to protect their own interests
enhancements: Serious physical injury (aggravated, Class D Felony)
notes: Mandatory reporting under 31 Del. C. § 3910. Includes physical, emotional, and financial abuse.

statute_title: Possession of a Deadly Weapon by a Person Prohibited
offense_class: Class F Felony (basic); Class D Felony (violent felony prior)
elements: Defendant possessed a deadly weapon
Defendant was a convicted felon, juvenile delinquent, or otherwise prohibited person
notes: Delaware requires a concealed carry permit for handguns. Prohibited persons include felons, those committed to mental institutions, and domestic violence misdemeanants.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
offense_class: Class F Felony (non-violent prior); Class D Felony (violent felony prior)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm or destructive weapon
Defendant had been previously convicted of a felony
notes: Applies to all convicted felons. Prior violent felony elevates from Class F to Class D.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Deadly Weapon Without a License
offense_class: Class G Felony (first); Class D Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed deadly weapon
Without a valid Delaware concealed carry license
notes: Delaware requires a concealed carry license. First offense is Class G Felony. Subsequent offenses are Class D Felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree)
elements: Defendant recklessly engaged in conduct creating a substantial risk of death or serious physical injury
By discharging a firearm
enhancements: Discharge into an occupied dwelling (first degree)
notes: Reckless endangering in the first degree (§ 604) is a Class D Felony. Second degree (§ 603) covers lesser reckless conduct.

offense_class: Class D Felony (over $1,000); Class F Felony ($500-$1,000); Class G Felony ($250-$500); Class A Misdemeanor (under $250)
penalty_max: 8 years (Class D); 3 years (Class F); 2 years (Class G); 1 year (Class A Misd.)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, produced, possessed, used, or transferred identifying information of another person
Without authorization
With intent to obtain benefit, credit, or other item of value
notes: Degree based on value obtained. Mandatory restitution.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree based on value
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over the property
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. Embezzlement is a theory of theft.

offense_class: Class E Felony (first degree — government/financial); Class G Felony (second degree — deeds/wills); Class A Misdemeanor (third degree)
penalty_max: 5 years (first degree); 2 years (second degree); 1 year (third degree)
elements: Defendant with intent to defraud, deceive, or injure
Falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
notes: Three degrees based on type of document. First degree covers government and financial instruments.

offense_class: Same class as forgery degree
elements: Defendant possessed a forged instrument
Knowing it to be forged
With intent to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting of currency is primarily federal. State charges cover forged documents.

offense_class: Same as theft by value tier
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant issued a check or other payment order
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Classified by amount using the same value tiers as theft.

offense_class: Class E Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly and with intent to defraud
Presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim
To an insurance company
notes: Class E Felony. Mandatory restitution. Investigation by the Delaware Insurance Commissioner.

statute_title: Unlawful Use of a Credit Card
offense_class: Class G Felony (over $500); Class A Misdemeanor (under $500)
elements: Defendant used a credit card or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, revoked, or canceled
To obtain goods, services, or anything of value
notes: Delaware has specific credit card fraud provisions. Value threshold determines misdemeanor vs. felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony
fine_max: $100,000 or twice the value of the property
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of specified unlawful activity
With knowledge that the property represents proceeds of unlawful activity
notes: Class D Felony. Fine may be twice the value of the property involved.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree based on value
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant obtained property by creating or confirming a false impression
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Fraud charged as theft by false pretense under the general theft statute.

statute_title: Unlawful Sexual Contact in the Second Degree
offense_class: Class G Felony (second degree); Class F Felony (first degree)
elements: Defendant had sexual contact with another person
Without the victim's consent
Or the victim was incapable of consent
enhancements: Use of force or coercion (first degree, § 769A)
Defendant in position of trust or authority
notes: Delaware uses 'unlawful sexual contact' for non-penetration offenses. Rape statute covers penetration offenses.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
Without the victim's consent
By use of force or threat
notes: First-degree rape has a 15-year mandatory minimum. Four degrees of rape. Sex offender registration required. No statute of limitations.

statute_title: Indecent Exposure in the Second Degree
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (second degree); Class A Misdemeanor (first degree)
elements: Defendant exposed their genitals or buttocks or her breasts
To a person who was not a member of the defendant's household
Under circumstances in which the defendant knew the conduct was likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Exposure to a child under 16 (first degree, § 765)
notes: Second degree is general indecent exposure. First degree involves exposure to a child under 16.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant engaged in or offered to engage in sexual conduct
In exchange for a fee
enhancements: Patronizing a minor for prostitution (enhanced felony charges)
notes: Both the person offering and the patron can be charged. Patronizing a prostitute is a separate offense.

offense_class: Class B Felony (production); Class D Felony (distribution); Class F Felony (possession)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, distributed, or produced material depicting a child engaged in a prohibited sexual act
Defendant knew the character and content of the material
notes: Federal charges common. Sex offender registration required. Production carries 2-year mandatory minimum.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
offense_class: Class G Felony (first); Class E Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Sex Offender Registry
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration
notes: Must register within 3 business days. Delaware has a tiered registration system.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
Victim was under 16 years of age
Defendant was 30 years of age or older
notes: Age of consent in Delaware is 18 (16 with close-in-age exception). Fourth-degree rape covers scenarios where defendant is significantly older. Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally caused public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
Or recklessly created a risk thereof
By engaging in fighting or violent behavior, making unreasonable noise, or using obscene language in public
notes: Common add-on charge. Often paired with resisting arrest.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent a law enforcement officer
From effecting a lawful arrest of the defendant
enhancements: Physical injury to officer (additional assault charges)
notes: It is no defense that the arrest was unlawful. Physical resistance causing injury may lead to additional assault charges.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, impaired, or hindered
The administration of justice
notes: Covers interference with court proceedings, investigations, and law enforcement functions.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disruptive behavior in the courtroom
Or failed to appear as ordered
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive; civil contempt is coercive.

statute_title: Consumption of Alcohol on Public Streets
offense_class: Violation (fine only)
elements: Defendant consumed alcoholic beverages on a public street or sidewalk
Or appeared in public in an intoxicated condition
notes: Delaware treats public intoxication primarily as a civil/health matter. May be taken to a detoxification facility.

offense_class: Class E Felony (felony case); Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Required to appear at a specified time and place
Defendant knowingly failed to appear
notes: Bench warrant issued. Bond forfeiture in addition to criminal charges.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant reported false information to law enforcement
Knowing the information was false
Regarding a crime or emergency
notes: Class A Misdemeanor. False bomb threats or similar may be charged under separate terrorism-related statutes.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class E Felony (threat to cause serious public inconvenience or evacuate a building)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit any crime likely to result in death or serious physical injury
With intent to terrorize another person
Or to cause evacuation of a building, vehicle, or public place
enhancements: Threat to public building, school, or transportation (Class E Felony)
notes: Basic terroristic threatening is Class A Misdemeanor. Threats causing evacuations or targeting public buildings are Class E Felony.

offense_class: Class D Felony (first degree); Class A Misdemeanor (second degree)
elements: Defendant made a materially false statement under oath
In an official proceeding
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: First-degree perjury in an official proceeding is a Class D Felony. Second degree (§ 1222) covers other sworn statements.

offense_class: Class E Felony
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer any benefit
Upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's official action
notes: Both the giver and receiver can be charged.

offense_class: Class E Felony (second degree); Class D Felony (first degree, with force)
elements: Defendant escaped from custody or detention
Defendant was in lawful custody
enhancements: Use of force or weapon (first degree, § 1252)
notes: First degree involves force or a weapon. Second degree is escape without force. Third degree (§ 1254) covers absconding from community supervision.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class F Felony (aggravated, torture/killing)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly subjected any animal to cruel mistreatment
Or cruelly killed or attempted to kill any animal
enhancements: Aggravated cruelty (torture, mutilation) — Class F Felony
notes: Basic cruelty is Class A Misdemeanor. Aggravated cruelty is Class F Felony. Animal fighting is Class E Felony.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
penalty_max: Remaining suspended sentence on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke, modify, or continue probation. Graduated sanctions program for technical violations.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was released on parole or supervised custody
Defendant violated a condition of release
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Delaware Board of Parole makes revocation decisions.

statute_title: Liability for Conduct of Another — Complicity
offense_class: Same as principal offense
elements: Defendant aided, counseled, agreed to aid, or attempted to aid another person
In planning or committing an offense
With the intent required for the commission of the offense
notes: A person is legally accountable for conduct of another when they are an accomplice. Punished to same extent as principal.

offense_class: One class below the attempted offense; attempt of Class A Felony = Class B Felony
penalty_max: Varies — one class below the attempted offense
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step
Toward the commission of an offense
With the kind of culpability otherwise required for the offense
notes: Attempt reduces the offense by one class. Attempt to commit a Class A Felony is a Class B Felony.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Varies — one class below the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to engage in or cause conduct constituting a crime
Any party to the agreement committed an overt act in furtherance
With the intent to promote or facilitate the crime
notes: Conspiracy is one class below the target offense. Requires an overt act. Renunciation is a defense.
